title: Require status checks on the Compliance ruleset
description: The Compliance ruleset (20470865) enforces deletion, non_fast_forward and required_signatures but has NO required_status_checks rule. A PR can merge today with a red Validate gallery contract. Add: Validate gallery contract, Validate commit messages, Validate PR title, Test template.
design: Put the rule on Compliance, which has no bypass actors, so it binds axeptio-bot too — a release sync PR cannot self-merge while breaking the gallery contract. Review (20470883) keeps its bot bypass so sync PRs still merge unattended.
notes: SEQUENCING: apply only after test.yml is on master and Test template has reported on at least one PR. A required check whose workflow does not exist never reports, and every PR then sits permanently pending with no way to merge.

title: Port the headless template test runner from the tag repo
description: The 18 ___TESTS___ scenarios shipped in v1.1.0 have never executed. CI only proves they parse (check_tests) and are syntactically valid JS (node --check). Port lib/template.mjs, test/run-tpl-tests.mjs, test/template-lib.test.mjs, package.json + lockfile and .github/workflows/test.yml from axeptio-gtm-public-template (its PR #73).
design: Two changes are required versus a verbatim copy, because the sibling is a TAG and this is a MACRO: (1) runCode must RETURN the vm completion value — every scenario here does 'const variableResult = runCode(mockData)'; the sibling discards it. (2) getType must be added to the require() defaults — the sibling does not shim it, so an unmocked require('getType') yields an auto-spy returning undefined, and every cookie path in this template gates on getType(x) === 'object'. That fails silently by returning undefined rather than erroring.
acceptance_criteria: npm ci && npm test runs all 18 scenarios plus the parser unit tests. Mutating template.tpl breaks exactly the expected scenarios. validate-gallery.py still passes with package.json at the repo root. template.tpl unchanged, BOM intact.
close_reason: Ported with two MACRO-specific adaptations; mutation matrix of 8 confirms the suite fails when it should. Two coverage gaps found and closed by mutation testing: the legacy source default and the lzc1. short-circuit were both unfalsifiable as originally written.

title: The v1.1.0 behaviour change is not in the published gallery changeNotes
description: Legacy variable instances gained the cookie fallback on the v1.1.0 update, so a tag gated on 'this variable is undefined' now fires earlier on repeat visits. The published changeNotes carry only the two commit subjects. metadata.yaml versions[] is generated and must not be hand-edited, so the reachable channel is the Help Center article.
notes: Root cause: the warning needed to be in the commit body at the time, where release-please would have picked it up. Worth remembering for the next behaviour-changing release.

title: The 18 template scenarios have never run in the GTM Tests tab
description: v1.1.0 shipped and is live to publishers on Google's next crawl. The scenarios have only ever run under the local emulator / the headless runner, which shims the sandbox rather than being it. Import template.tpl into a scratch GTM container and run the Tests tab, then Preview against a page running the live widget.
acceptance_criteria: All 18 green in the GTM UI. Preview confirms: variable resolves from the cookie on Page View with the SDK loaded async; the vendor array SHRINKS with no stale trailing entry after withdrawing a vendor; consent_mode is undefined (not garbled) with compressUserCookie on and a cookie past 3072 chars.

title: Keep non-template changes out of the gallery release notes
description: Port the sibling's PR #66 change to scripts/update-metadata-version.mjs: a GALLERY_SECTIONS allowlist (BREAKING CHANGES, Features, Bug Fixes, Performance Improvements, Reverts), with buildChangeNotes() tracking the current '### ' heading and keeping a bullet only when its section is allowlisted. Today every bullet in the top CHANGELOG section is published to the public gallery listing, including merge-commit PR titles.
design: Allowlist, not denylist, so a new release-please section stays off the public listing until someone opts in — the safe direction for public content.

title: Add a logo header, badges and a field-level reference to the README
description: Port the sibling's README treatment (its PR #68 plus #64). Logo via a <picture> element with prefers-color-scheme — GitHub strips CSS from README SVGs so fill=currentColor does not work. Five badges: GTM Gallery listing, Release, License, Validate gallery contract, Test template. Then expand the body into a field-level reference: Installing, Configuration (signal / source / cookie-name fields), Related templates, Support, Versioning.
acceptance_criteria: Every badge URL fetched and confirmed to render the expected value before commit. The gallery listing URL is verified, not assumed.
notes: The License badge is load-bearing, not decoration: it renders GitHub's DETECTED licence, so a repeat of SUP-1008 becomes visible on the repo front page instead of taking a customer report ~24h to surface.

title: Pinned GitHub Actions are on deprecated Node 20
description: Every workflow run emits a deprecation warning: actions/checkout v4.3.0, actions/setup-node v4.4.0, actions/setup-python v5.6.0 and googleapis/release-please-action v4.4.1 target Node 20 and are being force-run on Node 24. Harmless today; breaks the release pipeline when GitHub drops the shim. The sibling repos share this tooling and need the same bump.

title: Gallery notes filter is partial - it filters by section not by commit type
description: Mirrors the sibling's own caveat (its bead gtm-1v8). The GALLERY_SECTIONS allowlist filters by CHANGELOG heading, so a fix(ci): commit still lands under Bug Fixes and reaches the public gallery listing. Filtering by conventional-commit scope would close it properly.
